narrative: The model estimates a 74% chance that you will leave your job, which is a high-risk prediction and is why the promotion is denied. This is not a judgment of your performance; it reflects the model’s view that you are likely to exit soon. The strongest factor was your overall years of experience: at 6–10 years, you have more total experience than the largest group of employees predicted to stay, most of whom have 1–5 years, and this pushed the prediction toward leaving. The second factor was your tenure in your current organization. Although 1–5 years in the current job is common among employees predicted to stay, this still added to the leaving risk in your case. The third factor was outside job opportunities. You reported none, and having no other opportunities was a staying signal—but it was not strong enough to offset the first two factors. Given that, the organization should discuss your career path and promotion criteria openly, review whether your role, support, recognition, and workload are sustainable, and agree on concrete retention steps. You should also clarify what development or reward would make staying worthwhile.
